# Verdict: REVISE **Overall Assessment**: The component implements the foundational "happy path" of accessibility (semantic landmarks and a visible skip link). However, it suffers from a classic "80% implementation" gap: while the skip link exists visually and scrolls the page, it fails to programmatically move focus into the main content area. Additionally, it lacks state communication for the active navigation item. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: 1. **Focus Shift Gap**: Predicted that the skip link would scroll but not shift programmatic focus (Confirmed). 2. **Active State Gap**: Predicted missing `aria-current` on nav links (Confirmed). 3. **Contrast Issue**: Predicted footer text might be borderline (Confirmed). --- ## Findings ### Major Findings (Significantly degrades experience) **1. Skip link fails to programmatically shift focus to main content.** - **Evidence**: `MainLayout.jsx:5` (``) and `MainLayout.jsx:20` (`
`). - **User Group**: Keyboard-only users, Screen reader users. - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order). - **Why this matters**: In many browsers and SPA environments, a fragment identifier (`#main-content`) scrolls the viewport but does not move the programmatic focus. A keyboard user who clicks "Skip to main content" will find their next `Tab` press takes them back into the navigation menu they just tried to skip, rather than into the first interactive element of the main content. - **Fix**: Add `tabindex="-1"` to the `
` element. This allows the element to receive programmatic focus via the anchor link without adding it to the natural tab order. ### Minor Findings (Friction but workaround exists) **2. Missing active page indicator in navigation.** - **Evidence**: `MainLayout.jsx:13-16` (`
  • ...
    • `). - **User Group**: Screen reader users, Cognitive accessibility users. - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) / WAI-ARIA Navigation pattern. - **Why this matters**: Sighted users often rely on CSS classes to see which page they are on. Screen reader users have no programmatic way of knowing which link in the list represents the current page. - **Fix**: Dynamically apply `aria-current="page"` to the anchor tag that matches the current route. **3. Potential low contrast in footer text.** - **Evidence**: CSS `.footer { color: #666; background: #f5f5f5; }`. - **User Group**: Low vision users. - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum). - **Why this matters**: `#666` on `#f5f5f5` provides a contrast ratio of approximately **4.5:1**. While this technically meets the minimum for normal text, it is exactly on the threshold. In different lighting or on lower-quality screens, this may be difficult to read. - **Fix**: Darken the footer text to `#595959` or darker to provide a safer margin above the 4.5:1 requirement. --- ## What's Missing (Gaps) - **Programmatic Focus Target**: As noted in Finding 1, the target of the skip link is not "focusable" by default. - **Reverse Skip Link**: For very long main content areas, there is no way for a keyboard user to jump back up to the navigation without tabbing backward through the entire page (WCAG 2.4.1). - **Language Attribute**: While this is a layout component, it's worth noting that if the `` tag lacks a `lang` attribute, screen readers may use the wrong voice profile for the content within this layout. --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | **MEDIUM** | Skip link behavior and active page state are critical for orientation. | | Keyboard-only | **HIGH** | The "Skip to main content" functionality is a primary keyboard requirement. | | Low vision | **LOW** | Contrast is borderline but generally acceptable; layout reflow is simple. | | Cognitive | **LOW** | Layout is predictable and clean. | | Vestibular | **LOW** | No animations present. | | Auditory | **LOW** | No media elements present. | | Environmental | **MEDIUM** | Footer contrast check required. | - **Screen reader user**: Will hear "Skip to main content, link." Upon activation, they will be scrolled to the main area, but if they press Tab, they may be teleported back to the top of the page depending on the browser's handling of fragment identifiers. - **Keyboard-only user**: The visual reveal of the skip link is excellent. However, the lack of programmatic focus shift makes the "Skip" action feel broken or redundant. --- ## Verdict Justification The verdict is **REVISE**. While the developer has checked all the "visual" boxes for accessibility (semantic tags, a visible skip link), they have missed the technical implementation detail that makes a skip link actually functional for keyboard users (`tabindex="-1"` on the target). Without this, the skip link is an "illusion of accessibility"—it looks correct to an auditor but fails the user in practice. **To upgrade to ACCEPT:** 1. Add `tabindex="-1"` to `
    `. 2. Implement `aria-current="page"` on the active navigation link. 3. Slightly increase footer text contrast for a safer margin.
